strongest_angle: An analysis of the maritime territorial dispute between Thailand and Cambodia over an overlapping 27,000 square kilometer Gulf of Thailand seabed claim holding $300 billion in resources, following October 2026 talks.

key_facts.fact: Thailand and Cambodia agreed to use a naval hotline and exercise restraint to ease maritime tensions after holding mediation talks at The Hague.
Cambodia sought international conciliation after Thailand pulled out of their 2001 agreement to exploit offshore oil and gas resources in a 27,000 sq km chunk of maritime territory.
The South-East Asian nations have for decades pushed rival claims over maritime territories and the demarcation of their 800km land border.
On September 15, the foreign ministers of Thailand and Cambodia delivered opening statements in Singapore before a conciliation commission constituted under UNCLOS.
